source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Cell: The Unit of Life
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Rudolf Virchow completed the classical cell theory by adding that
options: all cells arise from pre-existing cells
plants alone are made of cells
the nucleus is absent in animals
questions.explanation: Schleiden and Schwann stated that plants and animals are cellular; Virchow added omnis cellula e cellula.

questions.stem: A typical bacterial nucleoid differs from a plant nucleus because the nucleoid
options: is bounded by a double membrane
contains many linear chromosomes with histones
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA lies in a nucleoid region without a nuclear envelope or nucleolus.

questions.stem: The middle lamella that cements neighbouring plant cells is rich in
questions.explanation: The middle lamella is a pectin-rich layer, mainly calcium pectate, deposited at the cell plate.

questions.stem: Singer and Nicolson described the plasma membrane as a
options: fluid mosaic of lipids and proteins
questions.explanation: The 1972 fluid mosaic model treats the membrane as a fluid lipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

questions.stem: The outer membrane of the nuclear envelope is typically continuous with the
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope’s outer membrane joins the RER, linking the nucleoplasm with the ER lumen.

questions.stem: A chromosome with the centromere almost at one end, giving one very short arm, is
questions.explanation: Acrocentric chromosomes have a terminal-near centromere; metacentric ones have a median centromere.

questions.stem: Colourless plastids specialised for storing starch grains are called
questions.explanation: Amyloplasts are leucoplasts that store starch; elaioplasts store oils and chromoplasts hold pigments.

questions.stem: The inner mitochondrial membrane is folded into
questions.explanation: Cristae increase the surface area that bears the electron-transport chain and ATP synthase.

questions.stem: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the main site of
questions.explanation: SER lacks ribosomes and handles lipid metabolism, steroid synthesis and detoxification.

questions.stem: Eukaryotic cytosolic ribosomes are 80S and are built from
questions.explanation: 80S ribosomes = 60S large + 40S small subunits; 70S (50S + 30S) occur in prokaryotes and organelles.

questions.stem: Proteins that span the lipid bilayer from one face to the other are called
questions.explanation: Integral (intrinsic) proteins are embedded in or across the bilayer; peripheral proteins are loosely attached.

questions.stem: The protein disc at the centromere to which spindle microtubules attach is the
questions.explanation: The kinetochore assembles on the centromere and is the attachment point for kinetochore microtubules.

questions.stem: Choose the correct combination about plastids. I. Chromoplasts may develop from chloroplasts in ripening fruit. II. Chloroplast stroma houses the enzymes of the Calvin cycle. III. All leucoplasts contain chlorophyll a only.
questions.explanation: Plastids interconvert and the Calvin cycle is stromal; leucoplasts are colourless and lack chlorophyll.

questions.stem: The term ‘cell’ was first used after observing box-like compartments in cork by
questions.explanation: Hooke (1665) named the empty cork chambers ‘cells’; Leeuwenhoek later saw living microbes.

questions.stem: Which structure is present in a typical plant cell but absent from a prokaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Plastids are eukaryotic organelles; prokaryotes may photosynthesize with thylakoids but lack plastids.

questions.stem: Cytoplasmic strands that pass through pores in the plant cell wall and join adjacent protoplasts are
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are lined cytoplasmic channels through the wall; they unify the symplast.

questions.stem: In the fluid mosaic model, the lipid molecules of the plasma membrane are
options: fixed in a rigid crystalline lattice
able to move laterally within each leaflet
questions.explanation: Phospholipids diffuse in the plane of the bilayer, giving the membrane its fluidity.

questions.stem: Most ribosomal RNA of a eukaryotic cell is transcribed in the
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of rRNA synthesis and assembly of ribosomal subunits.

questions.stem: A chromosome with a median centromere and two equal arms is described as
questions.explanation: Metacentric chromosomes have a mid-placed centromere; telocentric ones have a terminal centromere.

questions.stem: Stacked disc-like thylakoids inside a chloroplast form a
questions.explanation: A granum is a stack of thylakoids; stroma lamellae connect neighbouring grana.

questions.stem: Mitochondrial DNA of plants is typically
options: linear and histone-packaged like nuclear DNA
circular and present in the matrix
absent in all living plant cells
questions.explanation: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes in the matrix.

questions.stem: The membrane that bounds the large central vacuole of a plant cell is the
questions.explanation: The tonoplast is the vacuolar membrane and controls transport into the cell sap.

questions.stem: Microtubules of the eukaryotic cytoskeleton are polymers of
questions.explanation: Microtubules are α/β-tubulin polymers; microfilaments are actin and many intermediate filaments are keratins.

questions.stem: Which statement about the plasma membrane is incorrect?
options: It is a fluid lipid bilayer with proteins.
It is made chiefly of cellulose microfibrils.
questions.explanation: Cellulose is the wall polymer; the plasma membrane is a phospholipid–protein bilayer.

questions.stem: Secondary constrictions that produce a satellite (SAT chromosome) are typically associated with
questions.explanation: SAT chromosomes carry nucleolar organiser regions at a secondary constriction.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement regarding cell organisation.
options: Mesosomes in some bacteria are plasma-membrane infoldings.
Higher plant cells generally lack centrioles.
The middle lamella is mainly calcium pectate.
Every living plant cell contains a pair of centrioles in a centrosome.
questions.explanation: Angiosperm cells lack centrioles; the mitotic spindle is organised without a centrosome of the animal type.
